definitions.explanation: The wife of one's older brother. Japanese has specific kinship terms that distinguish between different in-law relationships based on the relative age and gender of the sibling.

examples.japanese: {兄嫁|あによめ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧だ。
examples.english: My brother's wife is good at cooking.

examples.japanese: {兄嫁|あによめ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: I went shopping with my sister-in-law.

examples.japanese: {兄嫁|あによめ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{連|つ}れて→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧うち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遊|あそ}び→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{来|き}た→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: My brother's wife came to visit with the children.

notes:
⟦{兄|あに}→兄：00570_ani⟧ means 'older brother,' and ⟦{嫁|よめ}→嫁：03670_yome⟧ means 'bride' or 'wife.' Together, {兄嫁|あによめ} specifically refers to the wife of one's older brother. Japanese kinship vocabulary is more precise than English, distinguishing family relationships by birth order and side of the family.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {兄嫁|あによめ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{仲|なか}が{良|よ}い→仲が良い：20668_nakagayoi⟧ (to get along well with one's sister-in-law)
- {兄嫁|あによめ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{実家|じっか}→実家：03076_jikka⟧ (sister-in-law's parents' home)

RELATED KINSHIP TERMS:
- ⟦{義姉|ぎし}→義姉：17835_gishi⟧ — sister-in-law (formal; older brother's wife or husband's/wife's older sister)
- {弟嫁|おとうとよめ} — younger brother's wife
- ⟦{嫁|よめ}→嫁：03670_yome⟧ — wife, bride, daughter-in-law
- ⟦{姉|あね}→姉：00571_ane⟧ — older sister (blood relation)
